stem.text: A ball is thrown vertically up into the air. It rises to the top of its path before beginning to fall vertically downwards.

stem.alt: Hand holding a ball at the bottom, labelled starting position; a ball labelled midpoint of path and a ball labelled top of path, each above the hand with an upward arrow between them.

stem.text: Assume that the gravitational potential energy of the ball is zero at its starting position.
Which statement about the ball is **not** correct?

A.text: As it rises, its kinetic energy is transferred to gravitational potential energy.

B.text: At the midpoint of its path, its gravitational potential energy is equal to its initial kinetic energy.

C.text: At the top of its path, its kinetic energy is zero.

D.text: At the top of its path, its total energy is less than its initial total energy.
